subject: Post-call: on-prem (air-gapped) deployment constraints & maintenance plan

Subject: Post-call: on-prem (air-gapped) deployment constraints & maintenance plan

Hi Samuel / EdgeBio IT team —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and the items we committed to follow up on: 

Recap (high level):
- Requirement: fully air-gapped, on-prem Redwood Private deployment behind customer firewall (no outbound internet egress from inference nodes).
- Primary workload: high-throughput batch inference for genomics pipelines + low-latency interactive queries for researchers.
- Desired capacity: ~10 concurrent model instances, peak token throughput ~200M tokens/day.

Open/Action items we covered:
1) Hardware inventory and exact GPU model (you said Dell hosts; please send server SKU + GPU model + VMM/hypervisor details).
2) Maintenance & upgrade policy: how do you want OS/kernel and firmware patches applied? acceptable maintenance windows?
3) Remote support options while air-gapped (on-site engineer, secure jumpbox during maintenance windows, or bring-your-own-kms/HSM integration?).
4) Backup/restore and offline model update process (how will we deliver new model artifacts in an air-gapped environment?).
5) Compliance evidence: SOC2/Security artifacts we can provide and any additional checks on our side (we'll share SOC2 report and audit contacts).

Next steps (what I'll do):
- Please send the hardware inventory spreadsheet you referenced (templates attached by me: redwood-offline-deploy-checklist.pdf is attached for reference).
- I'll coordinate internal SOW/ops MOP draft with Marissa for a site-survey and propose an on-site visit or guided remote validation.
- Monica will review the technical constraints (GPU/quantization/compatibility) and get back with a short matrix of supported configurations.

Can you confirm your preferred weekly maintenance window (local timezone) and whether remote SSH-based maintenance is allowed during that window? Also please attach the HW inventory when you can.

Thanks — talk soon.

— Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.ai

Alex —

Thanks for the clear recap. Attaching the HW inventory (EdgeBio-HW-inventory.xlsx). A few clarifications from our side: 

- Hardware: Dell PowerEdge R760 servers, 2x NVIDIA L40S (48GB) per node in our initial rack. Hypervisor: VMware vSphere 8.0. We intend to run Redwood in bare-metal VMs but can provide SR-IOV where needed.
- Maintenance window: Prefer Saturdays 02:00-06:00 local (EST) for reboots/firmware updates.
- Remote support: We cannot allow persistent outbound connections from the inference subnet. We can provide a jumpbox in a DMZ with time-limited bastion access during agreed maintenance windows and an on-site engineer for initial setup.
- Model updates: We will accept signed artifact packages via encrypted USB handoff and ingestion by our infra team; DocuSign/SOW required for access procedures.

Open questions: 
1) Can Redwood's offline deploy process work with signed artifacts and no outbound checksum calls?
2) What's the minimum GPU RAM you recommend for the 13B LLM family with 8k context in quantized form?
3) What upgrade cadence do you recommend for security patches versus model runtime upgrades?

I'll loop in Purchasing (Jason) once we have a draft SOW and BOM.

Sam
Samuel White
Director, Infrastructure — EdgeBio Therapeutics
samuel.white@edgebio.com

From: alex_martinez

Subject: Re: Post-call: on-prem (air-gapped) deployment constraints & maintenance plan

Sam — great, thanks for the inventory and the maintenance window. Answers inline and next steps: 

- Offline artifacts: Yes — Redwood supports ingesting signed model packages (we'll provide an offline verification tool you run locally; no outbound calls required). We'll deliver a signed tarball and a separate signing-public-key file; your infra team validates signatures prior to deployment.
- Minimum GPU: Monica will confirm exact mem requirements, but for 13B quantized (4-bit) we typically recommend >=40GB GPU memory to keep a reasonable perf buffer; L40S (48GB) should be OK but we will validate with our runtime matrix.
- Upgrade cadence: Security patches (OS/firmware) are customer-controlled; we recommend monthly security updates with quarterly runtime patches. Model runtime updates can be staged in canary then rolled during your maintenance window. We'll include an explicit rollback MOP in the SOW.

Marissa / Monica — can you draft a short SOW skeleton and an offline MOP template for air-gapped installs that includes: acceptance criteria, jumpbox access procedure, artifact signing process, and rollback playbook? I've attached our checklist (redwood-offline-deploy-checklist.pdf) for your reference.

Proposed next steps (for Sam & EdgeBio):
- Sam to confirm bastion/jumpbox handoff process and sign-off on Saturday 02:00-06:00 EST as the maintenance window.
- Redwood to provide: offline signature verification tool, sample MOP (redwood-offline-mop-sample.docx), preliminary BOM + estimated licensing for dedicated-private SKU.
- Schedule site-survey call or onsite visit (link below).

I'll send a follow-up with calendar picks for a 60-minute site-survey.

— Alex
From: monica_patel
To: marissa_cole, alex_martinez
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 14:03:27 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call: on-prem (air-gapped) deployment constraints & maintenance plan

Quick technical notes for the SOW/BOM: 

- GPU guidance: For 13B models with 8k context, target 48GB+ GPUs for headroom; 80GB GPUs reduce cross-node KV tensor spills for sustained low latency. If EdgeBio is ok with slight perf variance, 48GB L40S should work with our q4_0/q4_1 quant profiles.
- Networking: SR-IOV + dedicated NICs preferred. Avoid NAT-ing inference nodes; use the DMZ bastion for management.
- Patch strategy: Redwood can bundle runtime updates as an immutable image that your infra team pulls from an internal artifact repo. We'll provide a checksum file to validate integrity offline.
- Ops runbook sections to include: pre-maintenance validation, model snapshot/backup procedure (local object store), rollback steps, and post-maintenance verification (latency/throughput smoke tests).

I'll prepare a 2-page technical appendix for the SOW and a sample rollback playbook. Marissa, please draft the commercial SOW items (pricing, onsite rate, travel) and I'll add the tech appendix.

— Monica
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
